slides.title: Calculating Bid-Ask Spread

slides.title: Garbage Collection Latency Spikes
slides.prompt: Why do high-frequency trading (HFT) systems in Python explicitly manage or disable cyclic garbage collection (`gc.disable()`) during market hours?
options: To eliminate unpredictable multi-millisecond stop-the-world pauses during order matching loops
To reduce CPU energy consumption during market closing
To bypass SSL certificate checks on exchange WebSocket feeds
To force memory allocation directly to persistent NVMe SSD drives
slides.correctAnswer: To eliminate unpredictable multi-millisecond stop-the-world pauses during order matching loops

slides.title: Vectorized Backtesting with NumPy
slides.prompt: Fill in the vectorized Pandas method used to calculate logarithmic returns from a series of close prices.
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np
returns = np.log(df['close'] / df['close'].___(1))

slides.title: Sharpe Ratio Risk Measurement
slides.prompt: What does a strategy's Sharpe Ratio quantify when evaluating quantitative backtest results?
options: Excess risk-adjusted return relative to portfolio volatility
The maximum percentage drawdown from peak to trough
The total count of winning trades versus losing trades
The speed of order execution in microseconds
slides.correctAnswer: Excess risk-adjusted return relative to portfolio volatility

slides.title: Zero-Copy Buffers with PyArrow

slides.title: Slippage in Strategy Execution
slides.prompt: What causes trade execution 'slippage' during backtest simulation comparisons against live trading?
options: Difference between expected order entry price and actual filled price due to market movement and latency
Errors caused by invalid API secret keys
Timezone misalignments between exchange servers and local clocks
Rounding inaccuracies when converting floating-point values
slides.correctAnswer: Difference between expected order entry price and actual filled price due to market movement and latency
